The warm step gives −q/e₀; every delayed step multiplies a nonzero e_k by −q/e_{k−1}², so every denominator is nonzero and signs alternate. For the normalized log amplitude u_k this is u₁=−u₀, u_{k+1}=u_k−2u_{k−1}; the displayed oscillatory solution has the correct initial data. The characteristic-root angle is irrational modulo π because 2cosθ=1/√2 is not an algebraic integer (its rational norm is −1/2). Both signs of the nonzero wave are attained bounded away from zero on recurrent open arcs; its amplitude grows as (√2)^k, proving both subsequential limits and the corresponding residual-norm claim. At balance the absolute error stays √q and signs alternate. The nontrivial first residual difference lies in span(a), so RD takes the exact scalar normal-equation step. At consistency the warm step alone suffices if terminated there; this does not assert that the literal quotient is subsequently defined. Read VERIFICATION.md and verify.py as text; the analytic argument proves the infinite claim, not the recorded finite rational tests.

value.rationale: The example is a useful caution about naively applying a consistent-system algorithm to inconsistent data. As a stand-alone new finding, however, the proposed scalar classification is a routine endpoint substitution in the existing exact ratio law, combined with a one-dimensional secant quotient; no distinct mathematical boundary beyond what those formulas already determine is established. The failure does not suggest the frozen formulas or the warning are false.
